newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Consolidating Belgian shares retain confidence.
newsitem.headline: Consolidating Belgian shares retain confidence.

text.p: The Bel-20 index of leading shares .BFX, which shed 0.4 percent on Monday, was likely to consolidate further this week on mild profit-taking and waning speculation in a handful of leading shares, dealers said.
"We'll probably consolidate further," said Gert De Mesure at Delen Bank. But the market remained well-supported and would hold up well in the weeks ahead, another trader said.

Dealers said that with Europe not concerned about EMU, eyes would be firmly on the U.S. for further guidance. The short-term omens were not looking good with the Dow .DJI off more than 30 points in early trade and bonds and the dollar also weaker.
The Bel-20 closed 0.42 percent lower at 2,351.62 points, four points off the intraday low but 13 points below the high.
About two million Belgian shares were traded, representing 3.7 billion francs in value.
The Bel-20 was primarily hit by banks Kredietbank (KB) and BBL, which both lost 2.2 percent at 14,200 and 9,340 francs respectively.

KB started weakening last Wednesday after the bank quashed merger speculation by re-affirming in a newspaper interview that it would prefer to remain independent. It was also hit by a downgrade to 'neutral' from 'accumulate' by Merrill Lynch.
BBL started slipping last Friday after its CEO said the so-called Great Belgian bank project -- a merger with Belgium's biggest bank Generale Bank -- had been put on hold.
One dealer said that if any major news had to be expected, it was more likely to come from BBL than from KB.
Last week's downgrade to 'underperform' from 'hold' by Salomon Brothers continued to haunt chemicals firm Solvay , which ended 1.9 percent lower at 21,175.
Dealers said the downgrade was now virtually discounted and the stock was unlikely to drop below 21,000 francs.
Retailer GIB, quoted at 1,545 francs one month ago, ended 2.6 percent lower at 1,700 francs in a technical reaction after its recent surge.
Dealers said GIB had benefitted in recent weeks from talk that its search for a partner for some of its businesses, particulary its DIY outlets, might come to fruition.
Investor interest was also fanned by a rumour that French Paribas might consider taking full control of its Belgian Cobepa subsidiary.
"This automatically put the spotlight on GIB," a dealer said.
Cobepa is currently the largest shareholder in GIB with 17.8 percent.
Another trader said there had also been speculation that Cobepa could wish to exit GIB.
